why: An engine version is a PROMISE about behaviour, so it must move whenever behaviour moves. This file pins each published engine version to the determinism fingerprint it decides with. tests/replay/test_engine_version_moves_with_behaviour.py fails if the running engine's fingerprint is not the one pinned for its version, and the only honest way to make it pass is to publish a new version - never to re-pin an old one.
discovered: 2026-09-03: adding the expected_value check moved the fingerprint cc482f27 -> da21b43c while engine_version stayed mizan-core/0.1.0. Replay of the 12 live records then reported NOT IDENTICAL, which reads as tampering, when the truth was that the engine had changed and had not said so.

mizan-core/0.1.0.note: 26 checks. Superseded by 0.2.0; records written under it replay under 0.1.0 only.

mizan-core/0.2.0.note: 27 checks: adds expected_value, which refuses a spread whose credit-to-width implies negative expectancy.
